I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life — more than fifty years now. My back isn't what it used to be, and my two sons are both working in Baoding. So I keep it simple and manageable. I have about 5 mu of flat irrigated land, same as always.

Everyone around here grows wheat in winter and maize in summer. That's what I grow too. The land rests from nothing — we put two crops on it every year. I know this rotation. I know when to water, when to spray, when the aphids come on the wheat in May. I don't need to experiment at my age.

For wheat I'll use the Jimai variety the seed station sells — it's not the fanciest hybrid but it performs reliably in our soil. For maize I switched to hybrid seed years ago because the yield is noticeably better. I use compound fertilizer at planting and add urea later by hand or hire the village tractor service for spreading. I probably use a bit more nitrogen than I should — my father did the same — but I'd rather not risk a thin crop.

I'll irrigate wheat four times: once to help germination in October, once before winter sets in, once at jointing in April, once more at heading. Maize usually gets rain in July and August but I'll water once if it's dry. I pay the irrigation district fee every year regardless.

For pesticides, I spray herbicide on the wheat after it emerges, then spray for aphids and powdery mildew in May. For maize, one spray for armyworm if I see it.

I'll have the village machinery cooperative do the rotary tillage before maize sowing — I can't operate the tractor anymore.
